enonce.question:
Complete the sentences with the correct modal verb (can, could, may, might, must, should).
1. You _______ (must / can) be quiet in the library. Talking is forbidden.
2. _______ (May / Should) I borrow your pen, please?
3. He _______ (could / must) swim when he was five years old.
4. Students _______ (should / might) respect their teachers.
5. It's raining outside. You _______ (must / could) take an umbrella.
Fill in the gap: 'When she was young, she ___ run very fast.' Use the past ability modal.
Complete with the correct modal: 'You ___ smoke here; it is forbidden.' (mustn't / don't have to)
Turn this active sentence into the passive (present simple): 'People speak English all over the world.'

Rewrite the following sentences in the passive voice. Keep the same meaning.
1. Someone stole my wallet yesterday.
2. They are building a new bridge in the city.
3. People should respect the environment.
4. The teacher will explain the lesson tomorrow.
5. Someone has broken the window.
Choose and justify: 'It is very late, so the office ___ be closed by now.' (must / can't). Which one and why?
Correct the mistake: 'He will can help you tomorrow.'
Rewrite using a modal in the passive: 'Workers must respect the safety rules.' Focus on the rules.
Transform to the passive (present perfect): 'Someone has broken the window.'
Rewrite in the passive (past simple): 'A young architect designed this museum.' Keep the doer with 'by'.
Write a short safety notice of three sentences for a school laboratory, using at least three modal + passive structures (for example 'must be worn').

Rewrite the following paragraph in the passive voice, omitting the doer when it is unimportant: 'The council will build a new library. Volunteers are painting the walls. They have already planted the trees.'

Read the text and answer the questions using modal verbs and passive voice where necessary.

Last year, a new law was passed in Tunisia. It says that:
- All students must wear a uniform at school.
- Schools should provide free meals to poor students.
- Teachers must respect students’ rights.
- The government might build more schools in rural areas.

Questions:
1. What must students do according to the new law?
2. What should schools do for poor students?
3. What must teachers do?
4. What might the government do in the future?
5. Rewrite the first sentence of the text in the passive voice.
Rewrite this weak thesis to make it clear and specific: 'Sport is good.'

Write a short paragraph (5-6 sentences) expressing your opinion on the following topic: 'Should students wear uniforms at school?' Use at least one argument to support your opinion and one counter-argument to show balance.
Match the function to the connector. Which connector shows CONTRAST: 'moreover', 'however', or 'therefore'?
Name the three main parts of an argumentative essay, in order.

Read the following argument and identify the main opinion, supporting arguments, and counter-argument. Then, write a balanced response (8-10 sentences) using the structure: introduction, argument, counter-argument, and conclusion.

Argument: 'Social media should be banned for teenagers under 16 because it exposes them to cyberbullying and misinformation.'

Your task: Write a response either supporting or opposing this argument, using at least two supporting points.
Complete the counter-argument with a suitable refutation connector: 'It is true that television can be educational. ___, most channels broadcast programmes with little real value.'
Write a topic sentence for a body paragraph defending this idea: reading books improves the imagination.
Improve this repetitive sentence by varying the opinion phrase: 'I think phones are useful. I think they help students. I think they save time.'
Put these stages of a body paragraph in the correct P.E.E. order: Example, Point, Explain.
Choose a more formal alternative for the informal sentence: 'Phones are a big no in class, if you ask me.'
Write a full introduction (three to four sentences) for an essay on the topic: 'Should teenagers be allowed to have a part-time job?' End with a clear thesis statement.

Write a persuasive letter (10-12 sentences) to your school principal arguing for or against the idea of extending school hours. Use at least three arguments to support your opinion. Include an introduction, body paragraphs with arguments, and a conclusion. Use formal language and proper letter format (date, salutation, closing).

Example format:
[Your Name]
[Your Class]
[Date]

Dear Principal [Name],

[Your letter]

Sincerely,
[Your Name]
Write one complete body paragraph (Point, Explain, Example) arguing that public libraries should stay open, using at least two connectors.
Choose the correct form: 'He is good at ___ (cook).'

Complete the sentences with the correct form of the verb in brackets (gerund or infinitive).
1. She enjoys (read) books in her free time.
2. They decided (go) to the beach yesterday.
3. He avoids (eat) junk food because it’s unhealthy.
4. We plan (visit) our grandparents next weekend.
5. My brother hates (wake up) early in the morning.
Choose the correct form: 'We decided ___ (visit) our grandparents.'
Choose the correct form: 'She enjoys ___ (paint) in her free time.'
Complete: 'Would you mind ___ (open) the window? It is very hot.'
Correct the mistake: 'I want going home now.'
Complete: 'The child refused ___ (eat) his vegetables.'

Choose the correct form (gerund or infinitive) to complete each sentence.
1. She stopped (to talk / talking) when the teacher entered the classroom.
2. I remember (to meet / meeting) him at the party last year.
3. They promised (to help / helping) us with our homework.
4. He can’t stand (to wait / waiting) in long queues.
5. We need (to finish / finishing) this project by tomorrow.
Explain the difference in meaning: 'He stopped smoking' versus 'He stopped to smoke.'
Complete with the correct form: 'Please do not forget ___ (call) the dentist tomorrow.'
Write four sentences about your habits and plans, using: 'enjoy', 'avoid', 'hope' and 'plan'. Use the correct form after each verb.

Rewrite the following sentences using the gerund or infinitive form of the verb in brackets to express the same meaning.
1. It is important that you study hard for your exams. (study)
2. He doesn’t like it when people interrupt him. (interrupt)
3. She can’t bear it when people are rude to her. (be)
4. It’s necessary for us to leave early tomorrow. (leave)
5. I don’t mind if you come late. (come)
Complete the paragraph with the correct forms: 'I am interested in ___ (learn) Spanish. I have decided ___ (take) an evening class, and I look forward to ___ (meet) new people.'

Complete the sentences with the correct form of the verbs in brackets. Use the first conditional (type 1).
1. If I ______ (study) hard, I ______ (pass) my exams.
2. She ______ (not/go) to the party if she ______ (feel) tired.
3. They ______ (call) you if they ______ (need) help.
4. We ______ (visit) the museum if it ______ (not/rain).
5. He ______ (not/forget) his keys if he ______ (be) more careful.
Complete the zero conditional: 'If you heat water to 100 degrees, it ___ (boil).'
Complete the first conditional: 'If it rains tomorrow, we ___ (stay) at home.'

Rewrite the sentences using the second conditional (type 2).
1. He doesn’t have enough money, so he can’t buy a new car.
2. I don’t speak French, so I can’t translate this document.
3. They don’t live near the school, so they don’t walk to school.
4. She doesn’t have a driving licence, so she doesn’t drive to work.
5. We don’t have time, so we don’t visit our grandparents every weekend.
Complete the third conditional: 'If they ___ (leave) earlier, they ___ (not miss) the train.'
Complete (type 2): If I ___ (be) rich, I ___ (travel) the world.
Correct the mistake: 'If I would have time, I would help you.'
Correct the mistake: 'If it will rain, we will cancel the match.'
Complete the second conditional: 'If she ___ (win) the prize, she ___ (buy) a new car.'
Complete the second conditional: 'If I ___ (be) you, I would apologise.'
Write one sentence of your own for each of the following: a first conditional about the weather, a second conditional about a dream, and a third conditional about a past regret.
Identify the type and complete: 'If you had told me about the meeting, I ___ (come).' Which conditional is this?

Complete the sentences with the correct form of the verbs in brackets. Use the third conditional (type 3).
1. If she ______ (study) harder, she ______ (pass) the exam.
2. They ______ (not/miss) the train if they ______ (leave) earlier.
3. He ______ (not/be) late if he ______ (take) a taxi.
4. We ______ (enjoy) the trip more if the weather ______ (be) better.
5. You ______ (not/get) sick if you ______ (wear) a jacket yesterday.
Complete each sentence about the same situation, keeping the meaning: (a) I do not have a bicycle, so I take the bus. (b) 'If I ___ a bicycle, I ___ the bus.'
Report this statement: They said, 'We will travel tomorrow.'
Transform the following direct speech into reported speech: 'I am reading a book,' she said.
Report this statement: He said, 'I am hungry.'
Choose 'said' or 'told': 'She ___ me that the shop was closed.'
Correct the mistake: 'He asked where did I go.'
Report this command: 'Close the door,' the teacher said to us.
Report this question: 'Where do you live?' she asked me.
Convert this direct speech into reported speech: 'We will visit our grandparents next week,' they told me.
Report this negative request: 'Please do not touch the paintings,' the guard said to the visitors.
Report this yes/no question: 'Are you ready?' he asked.
Report this short dialogue: Sara said, 'I bought this book yesterday and I love it.' She was speaking to Ali.
Change this direct speech into reported speech, including the time reference: 'I finished my homework yesterday,' he said.
You interviewed a classmate. Report three of her answers in reported speech. Direct answers: 'I want to become a doctor.' 'I am studying biology now.' 'I will apply to university next year.'
